# PriorityQueueExtractionShapeMismatch

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 5.3" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Match the priority queue extraction mode.

## Example

Finding:

```php{2}
<?php
$q = new SplPriorityQueue(); $q->insert("task", 5); $q->extract()["priority"];
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Match the priority queue extraction mode.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Track builtin SplPriorityQueue mode (default EXTR_DATA) and literal inserted data. Report indexing extracted/current/top values by data or priority when the proven extraction mode does not produce that field and the inserted data type cannot provide it. EXTR_BOTH provides both fields; EXTR_PRIORITY provides only priority itself. Report the indexed expression.
- The mode is proven only by `setExtractFlags` calls that always run before the extraction. A `setExtractFlags` call on the queue variable that merely may run first (inside a branch, a loop, a short-circuit or ternary operand, a nested closure or arrow function, or later in a loop that also contains the extraction) leaves the mode unknown. An `insert` call that merely may run first never proves the queue holds a value, but its data and priority still count as possible extracted shapes.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Flow facts require a reachable path with no intervening mutation, escaped alias, unknown call involving the tracked value or analysis-budget exhaustion. Uncertain facts cannot prove a violation.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Unknown inserted data (which may itself be an array), overridden extraction behavior or mode invalidated by unknown calls prevent a finding.
- A conditional or deferred mode change before the extraction, or a conditional insertion of non-literal data, prevents a finding. Calls that can only run after the extraction do not.
- Exclude shadowed builtin symbols, unresolved required types, incomplete syntax and unsupported PHP versions.

## Fix

No automatic fix. Choosing a repair requires runtime information, error-handling policy or a semantic decision.

All edits use exact byte ranges, preserve comments and evaluation order, and require syntax supported by the target PHP version. A fix must never add an evaluation or silently change unrelated arguments.

## PHP versions

Minimum PHP 5.3.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "PriorityQueueExtractionShapeMismatch": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore PriorityQueueExtractionShapeMismatch
```
